findings.quote: Section $7$ bars sharing protected work information to give an unfair private advantage.
findings.problem: Example 7 first introduces the substantive confidential-information prohibition in its solution. Core Concept only names Sections 7, 8, and 9 as penalty categories. No supplied prerequisite or later-section reference teaches this offense before the learner must identify it.

checked: The lesson explains how salary-based ceilings differ from automatic sanctions, how notice and evidence support administrative decisions, how acts distinguish participation roles, and how statement-use purpose determines the remedy.

findings.quote: Helping an offender escape has further legal conditions. Family exemptions may also matter, so do not ignore a stated relationship.
findings.problem: The lesson tells students that escape assistance and family exemptions have conditions but never states those conditions or which relationships and acts qualify. These are limitations of the accessory rule taught here. No prerequisite or later explanation supplies them.
